lines: If you smell <wavy>smoke</wavy>, that is supper being planned properly.
Give the smokehouse room. Butchery works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the smokehouse. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
There you are. I was just near the smoker, trying to keep the day sensible.
Morning. Or afternoon. The work makes the hours blur if I let it.
Good to see you walking in calmly. That usually means nothing is on fire yet.
If you need me, speak up. If you need gossip, speak quieter.
You caught me before the next little disaster. That is rare timing.
Hello. Try not to bring the whole village into this unless it is important.
I have a moment. Not a long one, but a real one.
Come in, but mind the hooks and the smoke.
Morning. If you are hungry, you picked a dangerous place to stand.
I have clean hands, sharp tools, and a little time.
Step around the table. It has work on it.
Hello. The smokehouse is behaving, so I can talk.
You caught me before the next batch needs turning.
If you need something wrapped, wait until I finish this thought.
Careful where you lean. Everything has a purpose here.
Good to see you without a complaint about stew.
I can spare a moment while the smoke does its part.
Speak up. The cleaver is louder than manners today.
Welcome, if you washed your hands or at least your intentions.
I was counting stores. Try not to make me start again.
The day smells busy. What do you need?
Stand clear of the block and tell me your business.
